name: CONUS
long_description:
CONUS structures fragmented medical device information for surgeons. We combine manufacturer documentation, hospital protocols and medical research in one place, giving surgeons and MedTech teams reliable answers across products and procedures.

We already work with leading manufacturers including Johnson & Johnson, Stryker and Zimmer Biomet, and since launching six months ago we’ve gone live in 20 hospitals.

Long term, hospitals will use CONUS to select and order implants across manufacturers.
one_liner: The AI knowledge layer for medical devices

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer: CONUS started with five chief orthopedic and trauma surgeons who wanted better access to the information their teams need every day. The three of us had already worked together for years, combining backgrounds in AI, biomedical engineering and product development.

question_answers.question: How did you decide to apply to Y Combinator? What was your experience applying, going through the batch, and fundraising at demo day?
question_answers.answer: We met Tom Blomfield at a YC event at ETH Zurich, where he convinced us we were thinking too small about CONUS. That conversation set us on the path to building it full time and applying to YC.

question_answers.question: What's the history of your company from getting started until the present day? What were the big inflection points?
question_answers.answer: We started by bringing surgical information into one platform, then added CONUS Intelligence. Today, we’re live in 20 European hospitals, work with manufacturers including Stryker and Zimmer Biomet, and are expanding into the US.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer: Medical device knowledge is scattered across manufacturer PDFs, portals and hospital systems, leaving clinicians and field teams searching disconnected sources or calling someone who knows. As product portfolios and hospital-specific protocols multiply, finding reliable answers becomes harder for both the people using devices and the companies supporting them.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer: We want CONUS to become the knowledge infrastructure connecting medical device companies and clinical teams worldwide. Reliable product and clinical knowledge should be available in seconds, across specialties and wherever people work.

launches.title: CONUS: The AI Knowledge Layer for Medical Devices
launches.tagline: We structure fragmented medical device information for surgeons.
launches.body:
## **Surgery is complex. Finding answers shouldn't be.**

Modern surgery relies on complex implants and instruments. But manufacturer instructions, surgical techniques and hospital protocols are scattered across PDFs, portals and disconnected systems.

For a single procedure, surgeons may need to navigate multiple sources just to find the relevant information.

The knowledge exists. It just has no common home.

## How CONUS works

CONUS brings medical device knowledge into one place.

Surgeons can select a procedure, see which implant systems are available at their hospital and access manufacturer instructions, surgical techniques and hospital protocols.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=121625&key=user_uploads/3347806/fc56290e-fa4c-43ed-9c68-91b22dda1023)

**For medical device manufacturers,** CONUS provides a shared platform to make their product knowledge accessible to surgeons and equip field teams with structured information across their portfolios.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=121625&key=user_uploads/3347806/cfed0a0f-70fa-4f07-9402-4f8c90c298c8)

**CONUS Intelligence** makes this structured knowledge accessible through AI, providing answers backed by citations to the original sources.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=121625&key=user_uploads/3347806/67343f3b-d56a-4d11-9684-76ed1186352f)

## Built with surgeons. Growing with the industry.

**Developed with five chief surgeons**, CONUS is already live in more than 20 European hospitals just six months after launch and works with manufacturers including Stryker, B. Braun and many more.

We're building a growing, structured knowledge base across medical device portfolios, combining manufacturer information with hospital-specific systems and protocols.

And we're just getting started. Over time, we want this foundation to support how hospitals discover, evaluate and access medical devices across manufacturers.

## Our ask

We're now expanding into the US and would love to connect with medical device companies, particularly people in Sales, Marketing, Product and Field Service, as well as orthopedic surgeons and hospital leaders.

If you work in this space or know someone we should meet, we'd appreciate an introduction.
